forcedChoices.reason: The English billion is 10^9; Spanish «billón» is 10^12.

The English two billion is 2 x 10^9.

forcedChoices.choice: algo más que ... o algo diferente de ellas
forcedChoices.reason: Spanish needs different prepositions after «más» and «diferente», so the object moves to after the first phrase.
The English uses miles; the unit is kept, not converted.
The question begins at «how»; the concessive clauses before it are not part of the question.
The English uses «the total» against «the individual»; kept as a noun, distinct from «el todo» (the whole).
The English uses lowercase "he" for God; Spanish keeps the pronoun for clarity.
"becomes" shows a gradual change; "hacerse" carries it without a ser/estar choice.
